newsitem.title: INDIA: Repairs to burst India pipeline to take 4-5 days.
newsitem.headline: Repairs to burst India pipeline to take 4-5 days.

text.p: Supplies of crude oil to two major Indian refineries shut down after a pipeline burst will be resumed within four or five days following temporary repairs, Indian oil company officials said on Friday.

The refineries, at Bongaigaon in the northeastern state of Assam and Barauni, in the neighbouring state of Bihar, were shut down after crude oil spurting from the burst pipeline caught fire and blazed for seven hours on Thursday.
Officials said there were no casualties.
Indian petroleum sector officials said they did not expect a lengthy disruption of operations.
"I don't foresee any panic situation," A. Bhattacharya, economic adviser to the Ministry of Petroleum, told Reuters.

"We want to do temporary repairs as soon as possible within four to five days so that crude oil supplies begin," said M. Bhandari, chief engineer in charge of the pipelines of the state-run Oil India Limited (OIL).
The pipeline that burst at Hajo, 30 kms (19 miles) west of Guwahati, the capital of Assam, belongs to OIL, and supplies crude oil to the Guwahati, Bongaigaon and Barauni refineries.
Bongaigaon Refineries and Petrochemical Ltd has an annual capacity of 2.7 million tonnes but it currently processes about 1.6 million tonnes, officials said.
Barauni refinery is owned by the Indian Oil Corp, the country's largest oil refiner. It has an annual processing capacity of 3.3 million tonnes.

"There will be only two days of crude distillation loss in the Bongaigaon refinery if repairs are done in the next three to four days," an OIL official, who did not to be identified, told Reuters in New Delhi.
"Once normal supplies are resumed we will make it up. There will not be any loss in the throughput," he added.
Supply to the Guwahati refinery, upstream of where the break took place, was not affected, the official said.
Secondary units at Bongaigaon refinery have a storage capacity of about 15 days and are not likely to be affected by the oil pipeline burst, he said.
Officials of the Barauni refinery could not be reached for comment.
Officials said both refineries processed domestic crude for petroleum products sold on the domestic market.
The crude oil pipeline starts from Dhuliajan in Upper Assam and terminates at Barauni in Bihar.
OIL's Bhandari said on Thursday that reports of two explosions before the fire led him to suspect separatist insurgents triggered the pipeline burst and the ensuing fire.

He said he suspected the bombs were planted by separatist militants. Several separatist militant groups are fighting either for a separate homeland or independence in the remote northeastern state of Assam.
